title: Quality of Food
canonicalText:
[[PA.5051 | Quality of Food | Applies to: PACE | Revised 03/01/2024]]
<<page 1>>
I. PURPOSE
This policy outlines the standards for the quality of food served at the CalOptima Health Program of All-
Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE) Center.
II. POLICY
A. CalOptima Health PACE Centers shall provide meal services that meet the individual nutritional
  needs of the Participants and are of high quality.
B. CalOptima Health PACE Centers shall serve nourishing, palatable and well-balanced meals in a safe
  manner.
III. PROCEDURE
A. CalOptima Health PACE Center standards for quality of food are as follows:
  1. All food shall be of good quality.
  2. Foods (including nutritional supplements and nutrition support items) are procured from sources
    approved, or considered satisfactory, by Federal, State, Tribal, or local authorities with
    jurisdiction over the service area of the organization.
  3. Food in unlabeled, rusty, leaking, broken containers or cans with side seam dents, rim dents or
    swells shall not be accepted, retained or used.
  4. Home-canned foods shall not be used.
  5. All food shall be prepared and served at the proper temperature.
  6. Milk, milk products, and products resembling milk shall be processed or manufactured in milk
    product plants, meeting the requirements of Division 15 of the California Food and Agriculture
    Code.
    a. When milk is served as a beverage it shall be pasteurized, Grade ‘A’ milk or certified milk
      unless otherwise prescribed by a provider;
<<page 2>>
    b. Powdered milk shall not be used as a beverage but may be used in cooking;
    c. Instant liquid substitutes may be used only when dispensed from their original containers;
    d. When milk is served in individual containers, the cap or seal shall not be removed except in
      the presence of the Participant; and
    e. Milk may be served from an approved dispensing device and shall be dispensed directly into
      the glass or other container from which the Participant drinks.
  7. Meat, poultry, and meat products shall not be used unless they have met inspection standards of
    state or federal authorities.
B. The CalOptima Health PACE Dietician, or designee, shall conduct periodic food safety and sanitation
  audits to ensure compliance and report any issues for follow-up action to the CalOptima Health PACE
  Quality Improvement Department.
  1. If a contracted vendor provides the food service, the CalOptima Health PACE Dietary Supervisor,
    or designee, shall ensure that such vendor has conducted periodic food safety and sanitation audits
    and may request the results of such audits.
V. REFERENCE(S)
A. California Food and Agriculture Code, Division 15. Milk and Milk Products Act
B. CalOptima Health PACE Program Agreement
C. Federal Register Volume 64, No. 226
D. Title 22, California Code of Regulations (C.C.R.), §78323
E. Title 42, Code of Federal Regulations (C.F.R.), §460.78
<<page 4>>
IX. GLOSSARY
PACE Center: The location designated by CalOptima Health PACE at which Participants shall receive PCP services.
Participant: An individual enrolled in the CalOptima Health PACE program.
Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE): PACE is a long-term comprehensive health care program that helps older adults to remain as independent as possible. PACE coordinates and provides all needed preventive, primary, acute and long-term care services so seniors can continue living in their community.
